## v0.6.0 amendment

The optional browser experiment was rejected. Sparse correction is absent from the
browser protocol, UI, Wasm surface, and ordinary web build. Research-only policy and
kernels are consolidated under the non-default Rust `validation` module.

| Current contract | State |
| --- | --- |
| Browser sparse correction | Removed; retained only in the non-default Rust validation module |

## Post-v0.5.0 amendment

A visual diagnostic found that bounded sparse correction primarily adjusts `ANI_c`
inside already-visible, highly similar low-cardinality repeat blocks. It did not show
a compelling structural-recovery benefit, so the mode remains disabled by default.
The browser toggle described here was an intermediate experiment and is superseded by
the v0.6.0 amendment above.

| Historical post-v0.5.0 experiment | State |
| --- | --- |
| Browser sparse correction | Optional Advanced options toggle; disabled by default |

## v0.2.1 amendment

The assertion-backed browser-default gate now tests the complete 256- and
1,024-register, HLL-p10, sparse-disabled production pipeline against complete canonical
k-mer sets. Release errors are reported only after applying the displayed
`ANI_c=C^(1/k)` transform. The fixed production path passes its preregistered mean,
P95, 0.80-floor crossing, missing-value, and direction gates. Sparse correction remains
disabled in the browser because the accepted defaults pass without its runtime cost.

The bounded estimator report now emits `ANI_c` variance and union-occupancy statistics
and asserts the selected 256/1,024-register HLL-p10 rows. The legacy estimator and fused
projection APIs are deprecated for removal or validation-only isolation in v0.3.0.

Current estimator-report columns: `estimator`, `registers`, `hll`, `mean_abs_ani_c`,
`p95_abs_ani_c`, `ani_c_bias`, `ani_c_error_variance`, `mean_union_occupancy`,
`minimum_union_occupancy`, `fn80`, `fp80`, `fn85`, `fp85`, `fn90`, `fp90`, `fn95`,
`fp95`, `diagonal_holes80`, `one_pixel_holes85`, `isolated_false85`,
`forward_continuity85`, `reverse_continuity85`, `local3_error`, `local5_error`,
`neighbor_error_corr`, `top_feature_overlap`, `component_count_error85`,
`fingerprint_collisions`, `comparison_ms`, `selected_config_gate`.

## v0.2.0 amendment

The original decision was accepted during the beta hardening cycle. The final v0.2.0
release supersedes decision 5, the high-sensitivity clause of decision 9, and decision
13 while retaining them below as historical context.

| Historical v0.2.0 contract | State |

The browser uses uncertainty-selected detailed refinement only. The sparse-correction

rendering, panning, direct reordering, and disabling.

The original evidence paragraph incorrectly named occupancy as an emitted estimator
report column in v0.2.0. That omission is corrected by the v0.2.1 report above.

Historical v0.2.0 estimator-report columns: `estimator`, `registers`, `hll`, `mean_abs_ani`,

`diagonal_holes80`, `one_pixel_holes85`, `isolated_false85`, `forward_continuity85`,

All-family browser automation now passes in Chromium, Firefox, WebKit, and installed

## Context

An external review of v0.1.0 identified scientific-path drift, a hash-based “exact”
oracle, stale worker transactions, initially incorrect terminal dispatch, duplicated
prepared memory, avoidable tile copies, blocking annotation parsing, missing browser
tests, dispersed parameters, and obsolete candidate implementations. It also proposed
verified OPH winners, lower HLL precision, uncertainty-led refinement, pooled direction
evidence, and display-aligned validation.

The original OPH paper defines the matched-bin estimator as `Nmat/(k-Nemp)`, equivalent
here to verified matches divided by union-occupied registers when fingerprint
verification is collision-free. Because a 32-bit fingerprint has a small but nonzero
whole-matrix collision risk, this was treated as a candidate pending validation.

## Decision

1. Production hashing is canonical ntHash2 only.
2. Production similarity uses undensified OPH and
   `verified_matches/union_occupied`; 14 low planes are only a comparison prefilter.
3. HLL precision is 10.
4. The default progressive tiers are 256 registers, then 1,024 registers.
5. *(Superseded by the v0.2.0 amendment.)* The default display floor is 85%.
   Optional high-sensitivity mode exposes the bounded sparse correction near 80%; it
   is off by default.
6. The display score remains the maximum of both directed containment estimates,
   transformed as `ANI_c=C^(1/k)`. `ANI_c` is not asserted to be biological ANI.
   Direction evidence is pooled and its display chroma depends on support.
7. Exact distinct canonical two-bit k-mer sets are the sole scientific oracle.
8. Every numeric tile is identified by an immutable validated `ScientificConfig`
   digest.
9. *(High-sensitivity clause superseded by the v0.2.0 amendment.)* Quick and detailed
   builds remain separate. Completed quick blocks paint during axis preparation. After
   preview paint, detailed blocks replace compatible quick blocks individually as they
   finish. Only display-uncertain tiles receive the detailed tier by default;
   high-sensitivity mode refines the complete request.
10. Mutable build sketches are frozen before retention; session, prepared-axis, and
    zoom-axis allocations are admitted against explicit budgets.
11. FASTA state mutations are serialized and transactionally committed by generation.
12. Phase 0, minmer/bottom-s, alternate-hash/Murmur, densified OPH, inverted-matrix,
    and legacy base kernels are removed. Git tag `v0.1.0` preserves them historically.
13. *(Superseded by the v0.2.0 amendment.)* BED/GFF/GTF import and feature tracks are
    removed before the v0.2 beta because the implementation did not meet the release
    reliability bar. The v0.1.0 tag preserves that experiment historically.

## Evidence

The release-mode estimator sweep covers registers 256/1,024/2,048, HLL p8–p12, both
estimator formulas, production seed zero plus validation-only seeded ntHash2 layouts,
several sequence realizations, random 80–99% identities, repeats, and cardinality
imbalance. It reports error, bias, zero inflation, four threshold confusion matrices,
spatial continuity/component/neighborhood diagnostics, runtime, and
32-bit/full-winner discrepancies.

At 1,024 registers/HLL p10, mean and P95 absolute ANI error changed from
0.008350/0.026505 for the legacy formula to 0.008108/0.025736 for verified winners.
At 2,048/p10 they changed from 0.005073/0.022071 to 0.004798/0.020423. These numbers
use four genuinely distinct hash layouts and supersede the earlier repeated-layout
figures. No tested
fingerprint discrepancy was observed. HLL p10 preserved display decisions relative to
p12; p8 was less stable.

An exact coarse projection from 2,048 to 256 registers was implemented and benchmarked.
On an 8 Mb, 1,000-cell native release fixture, separate builds took 139 ms to preview
and 672 ms total. Detailed build plus projection took 591 ms total but 533 ms before a
preview could exist. The interactive product therefore keeps separate builds.

## Consequences

The maintained backend is smaller, config drift is detectable, exact validation no
longer shares the production hash, and default initialization/memory cost is lower.
Preview variance is intentionally visible and later replaced. The 85% default reflects
the signal budget rather than hiding a claim that 80% is uniformly reliable.

At the time of the original decision, the results justified a functional preview, not
research-validation language. Broader biological/multi-realization spatial validation,
all-family browser testing, and current chromosome-scale memory/performance reports
were still release gates; the amendment records which of those gates v0.2.0 completed.
